An idea for a cool new app. A business idea you thought of at 1am in the morning, built out halfway, and never looking back at again. It's not you — it's that starting something and finishing something are two very different things, and it's normal to excel at one or the other and not always both. Sitting on your phone in your notes app, your idea isn't worth anything to anyone, including you. Espalier is where you can go to pass it on to someone who believes in your idea and can bring it to life.

How it works

Some of us love to start things but not finish them.
Some of us love to finish things but not start them.
And both are okay.

Espalier connects starters with finishers to bring incredible ideas to life that might otherwise just sit on the sidelines — freeing both to do what they actually do best. And both sides get to make real money from it.

If you're a starter

You've got no shortage of ideas — the hard part is ever finishing one. Here's exactly what happens when you list one here.

01

Tell it like it is

Describe it in your own words. Attach files, drop in a voice memo, add links — whatever shows the real thinking you've already put in.

02

Get scored, not judged

Espalier's own AI models check for one thing: a genuine, thought-out attempt. Not polish, not perfection — real effort.

03

Approved — or a second look

Most genuine ideas go live right away. If one's flagged, you'll see exactly why.

04

Live in the marketplace

Finishers looking for exactly this kind of thing can find it and reach out.

05

Sign a deal, keep a stake

Cash now, an ongoing share, or both — you're locked in for whatever it becomes.

If you're a finisher

Starting from zero is the part you dread — but handed a half-built idea with real bones, you're unstoppable. Here's how it works.

01

Browse real progress

Every listing already has real work behind it — not just a raw idea someone jotted down.

02

See exactly where it stands

A forecast score, what's built and what's not, what it'd cost to finish, and why.

03

Propose your terms

Cash upfront, an ongoing share, or a mix of both — whatever fits the work ahead.

04

Sign and take it over

Once terms are agreed, the idea — and everything behind it — is yours to run with.

05

Build it, launch it, keep the majority

Do the real work, launch it, grow it — and keep the lion's share.

Why it's worth trusting

You can trust us — here's exactly why.

Every listing is assessed by Espalier's own proprietary AI models, built specifically for this, not a generic off-the-shelf tool.

For starters — 3 of many

Every idea is timestamped

The moment you list something, Espalier records exactly when — real proof of when you shared it, protecting your claim to the idea itself.

Details stay locked until someone commits

The title and pitch are public. The files, links, and real specifics only open up once a finisher is serious enough to commit to a conversation.

Every finisher carries a reputation

Before you ever say yes, you can see a finisher's track record — completed deals, follow-through, how they've treated other starters.

For finishers — 3 of many

The Espalier Score

Custom-built AI models score every idea on real signals — readiness, cost to finish, profit potential — not on how good the pitch sounds.

Claims get checked

What a creator says is built gets checked by our own AI against the actual files and links — so "80% done" means something.

Every starter carries a reputation too

A history of honest, accurate listings builds up over time — so the strongest starters stand out to you before you even reach out.

How the money works

Pre-built templates — catered to each idea and each person.

The two of you agree on terms before anything changes hands or any proprietary information related to the idea is released. Espalier doesn't set the split — but we have our AI models recommend deal formats and conditions directly relating to all the information we have about a given idea. We always make sure both parties have all the relevant details they need to enter an agreement with transparency, good faith, and backup precautions in case there is any discrepancy between what someone commits to or offers and what they are actually able to provide.

Template 1
Cash on signing

A one-time payment for taking the idea over — negotiated based on how far along it is and what it'd take to finish. Certainty now, nothing owed later.

Template 2
Ongoing revenue share

The original creator keeps a percentage of future revenue — no cash upfront, but real upside if it takes off.

Template 3
Cash + ongoing share

The most common structure — a smaller upfront payment plus an ongoing share, balancing certainty now against upside later.

Template 4
Advisory role + share

The starter stays involved as a consultant or advisor while the finisher builds, keeping a revenue share in exchange for staying available.

Template 5
Milestone-based payout

Cash is released in stages as the finisher hits agreed milestones — lower risk for the finisher, steady payout for the starter as real progress happens.

What Espalier itself charges
Platform safety

We assume good intent on every user's end.
That doesn't mean we skip the guardrails.

Every idea is reviewed before it goes live, and listings that don't meet our criteria aren't accepted until they do. Every account carries a visible track record. Timestamps are generated for every posted idea, protecting a creator's claim to it. Proprietary details are only shared once both sides are genuinely committed to a deal. And every finisher has to agree to a set of platform terms before they can even browse — including explicitly committing to never use the platform to study and then build someone else's idea without them. That's the baseline, not the whole list.

Quick answers

Curious minds think alike.

Do I still own my idea once I list it?

Yes, right up until you sign a deal with a specific finisher on terms you agreed to. Listing something changes nothing about who owns it.

What if nobody claims my idea?

It just stays listed. There's no penalty for an idea that hasn't found its person yet — some take longer than others to find the right match.

What happens if a finisher doesn't follow through?

If they don't hold up their end of the agreement, it affects their reputation score within the platform. However, one part of handing over an idea to someone else is giving up control, and understanding that the finisher can then act on and finish the idea in their own way.
